newsitem.title: USA: Mellon sees good fit with California bank.
newsitem.headline: Mellon sees good fit with California bank.

text.p: Keith Russell, Mellon Bank Corp vice chairman and head of Mellon Financial Group-West Coast said Monday Los Angeles-based business lender 1st Business Bank is a great fit with Mellon.
Mellon earlier announced it had signed a definitive agreeement to acquire 1st Business Corp, parent of the California bank, in a stock transaction.
The purchase price was not disclosed. Focusing on mid-sized businesses, 1st Business Bank has about $1.1 billion in assets.
Russell said in a telephone interview that 1st Business Bank's deposit-taking capability and strong position in middle market banking "fits very nicely" with Mellon's growth strategy.

Russell said the acquisition will be known as Mellon 1st Business Bank and will continue to operate as a separate banking entity. He said Mellon will study what is the appropriate charter for the unit to have and in the meantime it will operate with a state charter.

Robert Kummer, 1st Business chairman and chief executive, said the transaction is not driven by cost reductions. "There is a teriffic strategic fit here," he said. "This is a great opportunity to take Mellon's capabilities and expand further out here."

In the telephone interview, John Anderson, the Southern California businessman who owns 1st Business Corp, said the decision to sell followed a telephone call two or three months ago from Mellon Chairman, Chief Executive and President Frank Cahouet. He said the call led to talks that resulted in the deal announced Monday. Anderson said there had been many inquiries about selling 1st Business over the past few years.
Anderson, known as an entrepreneur and civic leader, will remain on the board of directors at Mellon 1st Business Bank.
Anderson said the California economy is "positive" right now with vigorous activity in the north and the Los Angeles-San Diego area "really on the move."
He said the rebound is driven by high technology, Pacific rim trade and a rapidly growing middle market sector.
